name: What Are the Key Steps in a Kitchen Plumbing Upgrade?

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Upgrading your kitchen plumbing, whether it's a small change or a big overhaul, involves a clear process to ensure everything works perfectly and safely. Here's a general outline of the key steps you can expect:

step.name: Step 2
step.text: **Step 1: Define Your Scope.** First, figure out exactly what fixtures you're upgrading or adding – new sink, faucet, dishwasher, disposal, or maybe a new water line. This determines the complexity of the project.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: **Step 2: Shut Off Water and Remove Old Components.** Before any work begins, the water supply to the area must be completely shut off. Then, any existing fixtures, pipes, and old components can be safely removed.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: **Step 3: Install New Supply and Drain Connections.** This is where the new plumbing goes in. Depending on your upgrade, this could involve new water lines, drainpipes, and connections for your chosen fixtures. Proper pipe sizing and drain slope are really important here to prevent future issues.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: **Step 4: Test for Leaks.** This step can't be skipped! Once everything is connected, the water is turned back on carefully, and every connection is thoroughly checked for leaks. You want to catch any drips before walls or cabinets are closed up.

step.name: Step 6
step.text: **Step 5: Confirm Code Compliance.** Especially if you've moved lines or added new ones, it's crucial to make sure all work meets local plumbing codes. This might involve inspections, depending on the scope of your project and your specific location in the East Bay.

step.name: Step 7
step.text: Following these steps helps ensure a successful plumbing upgrade. For reliable kitchen remodels and plumbing work in areas like Berkeley, Oakland, or Albany, Frasheski Construction has the expertise to get it done right.
